name: Abaddon
overview: Abaddon is a male figure described in Scripture as the king over the locusts and the angel of the abyss, as revealed in Revelation 9:11. His role is uniquely defined by his authority over these destructive forces. No tribal affiliation or additional personal details are provided in the biblical text.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Abaddon' means 'destruction' and is a proper name given by God, emphasizing his association with ruin and judgment. He is also called 'Apollyon,' another proper name given by God, which appears alongside Abaddon in Revelation 9:11. These names reveal his nature as an agent of divine judgment.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Abaddon beyond his role as king over the locusts and angel of the abyss. There are no other relational details provided in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Abaddon holds significant importance in the biblical narrative as a symbol of divine judgment during the end times. As the angel of the abyss and leader of the locusts, he represents the execution of God's wrath against the wicked. His presence in Revelation 9:11 highlights the reality of spiritual forces unleashed in the final tribulation, underscoring the seriousness of God's sovereign authority over evil.
